artifacts.summary: Documents that task 612's description is a verbatim duplicate of a separate, correctly-sited .dotfiles task's removal narrative; reconstructs task 612's real (extension-side, per-repo activation) scope from file_scope and codebase evidence, including a found lean-lsp precedent for the MCP-registration mechanism.

next_steps: Have a human confirm/correct task 612's stored description against this report's reconstructed scope, then run /orchestrate 612 to create an implementation plan grounded in that scope (not the description's literal removal content).

user_decision.question: Task 612's stored description is a verbatim duplicate of a separate .dotfiles task's (project 138) removal-work narrative, mismatched with task 612's own file_scope/title/siting (which all correctly identify it as the first-half, extension-side activation-surface task). How should this be resolved before planning proceeds?
options: Correct task 612's description field in specs/state.json to describe the actual first-half scope (reconstructed in this report's Findings), then proceed to planning normally
Leave the description as-is and have the plan phase treat this research report's Findings/Decisions sections as the authoritative scope statement, citing it explicitly rather than the description
Abandon/merge task 612 as a duplicate and re-file the first-half work under a fresh task with a correct description
user_decision.recommended: Correct task 612's description field in specs/state.json to describe the actual first-half scope (reconstructed in this report's Findings), then proceed to planning normally
user_decision.obligation: The corrected description must state task 612 is the extension-side, per-repo-activation-surface build (mirroring agent-system/extensions/lean's setup-lean-mcp.sh/lean-lsp-register-project.sh/install-lean-lsp-session-hook.sh triad, plus the settings-fragment.json permissions/hooks additions) and must not retain any instruction to edit .dotfiles-owned files (modules/home/services/sapience.nix, config/claude/settings.json, docs/sapience.md), which belong to the separate .dotfiles task 138.

memory_candidates.content: The lean extension (agent-system/extensions/lean) already implements a complete, working pattern for per-repository MCP-server registration triggered by extension presence rather than machine-wide nix activation: a stable user-level SessionStart hook (installed to $HOME/.claude/hooks/, never inside any single repo's disposable .claude/ tree) detects per-project applicability (lakefile.lean/lakefile.toml for lean) and calls a stable user-level writer script that registers/repairs that project's own .projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers entry in ~/.claude.json. Installed via a two-file idempotent --remove-capable install script (install-lean-lsp-session-hook.sh). This is the pattern to mirror for any future per-repo MCP server registration that must also work in a fresh git worktree with no .claude/ deploy at all.

lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua's settings merge engine already supports merging a Claude-Code-native hooks object (SessionStart/PreToolUse/etc. matcher-array shape) into a consuming repo's .claude/settings.local.json, not just permissions.allow -- with identity-based dedup (find_hook_match) and clean removal on unload (unmerge_settings/remove_orphaned_hook_registrations), including pruning an emptied hooks key to avoid Claude Code's rejection of a hooks:[] shape. Any extension wanting to ship per-repo hooks via settings-fragment.json's hooks key can rely on this as already-proven, not something to build.
